correctness.rationale: Writing z(w)=cw+d/w with 0<r=d/c<1 gives deck h(r/w)=h(w). Unimodularity of rational h on unit circle gives h(w)h*(1/w)=1 as a rational identity. Reflect and combine deck involution to force dilation h(v)=h(r²v). Any rational Laurent expansion around 0 then has only exponent zero because r² is not a root of unity; hence h constant unimodular. For polynomials, H=Q/P handles P≠0; P=0 forces Q=0 by infinitely many zeros. For degree≤n, |P(z(e^{it}))|² is a Laurent polynomial of order≤2n; a nonzero intensity difference has at most 4n distinct points on S¹. The ellipse parameter is injective, so 4n+1 samples force full equality. Reciprocal linear polynomials disprove the circle case. Checked identities and CHECK.py’s exact Laurent arithmetic; numerical samples are supplementary, not an infinite proof.
